lesson.subtitle: Lesson 4 -- Must, Should, May
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Adriana Cardoso Assunção | Lesson 4 -- Must, Should, May

listenings.text: Good afternoon. I am the compliance officer for the region, and I have ten minutes, so I will be direct. Three things are obligations, not recommendations. First, every manager must complete the psychosocial risk training before the end of the quarter. There is no exception for people who joined this year. Second, any grievance received in writing has to be answered in writing within five working days. Not a phone call. In writing. Third, nobody may investigate a complaint about their own team. If the complaint is about your area, it goes to me. Everything else in the document is guidance: you should document the conversation, and you should tell the employee what happens next, but nobody will discipline you for the format you use.

Hi Adriana, it is Paula from the legal team. I read the draft of the wellbeing policy and there is one thing you need to change before it goes out. In the section about workload, you wrote that managers should review the distribution of tasks every quarter. If that is what the duty of care requires, it cannot be should. It has to be must, or a lawyer will read it as optional in the first hearing we have. And the opposite is also true: in the paragraph about the anonymous channel, you wrote that employees must report any concern. Nobody can be obliged to report. That one has to become may. One word in each paragraph. Call me if you want to go through it together.
